description: Age-appropriate financial dashboards for Jordan and Casey, scoped to their individual Capital One Money accounts via the existing RBAC system. Kids log in with their own passphrase and see only their linked accounts. Parents see kids' accounts on the normal accounts screen, broken out like any other family member. Kids' balances are excluded from household coverage/liquidity calculations. Monthly LLM-generated 'Money Report Card' provides encouraging financial narrative.

timing.plannedEarliestExecution: now — gating conditions met (auth, budgets, categories all shipped)
timing.gatingCondition: None — Features 4 (budgets/categories), 6-auth (RBAC with parent/kid roles), and 12 (coverage/liquidity) are all complete.

principles: HARD DATA ISOLATION — kid sessions are denied at the API layer from accessing any data outside their account_members-linked accounts. All parent routes use requireParent middleware. This is enforced server-side, not just UI hiding.
Kid login must NEVER provide access to parent accounts, household finances, settings, Plaid Link, or magic actions
Use existing household categories — no kid-specific category taxonomy. Parents manage categories and category_rules; kids' transactions categorize through the same pipeline.
Kids' account balances are excluded from household coverage/liquidity calculations — their money does not cover parent liabilities
Keep it simple — teenagers need clarity, not complexity
Money Report Card should feel encouraging, not judgmental

SECRETS INVARIANT — Money Report Card LLM prompts contain only the kid's first name, transaction amounts, merchant names, and categories. Never access tokens, account numbers, .env values, or household financial data. Enforced by secrets-guard.

existingInfrastructure.auth: family_members.role (parent/kid), requireParent middleware, requireAuth middleware, session carries role — all shipped in Feature auth (migration 006)
existingInfrastructure.accountScoping: account_members table links accounts to family members — parent assigns kids' accounts via PUT /api/auth/account-members
existingInfrastructure.categories: Household category system with category_rules for auto-categorization — no changes needed, kids use same categories
existingInfrastructure.coverage: coverage-calculator.js queries all depository accounts — needs filter to exclude kid-owned accounts

techStack.database: PostgreSQL (existing schema, scoped via account_members join)
techStack.testing: node:test for data scoping and budget tests, manual testing on 2 dev boxes
techStack.llmProvider: OpenAI API (gpt-5-nano) for Money Report Card

userStories.title: Kid dashboard route and API-enforced data scoping
acceptanceCriteria: Express routes: /kids/:name serves kid dashboard (e.g., /kids/jordan, /kids/casey)
Kid API endpoints scope all queries through account_members for req.member.id
Kid session cannot access any parent route — all parent routes use requireParent middleware
Kid session cannot access sibling's data — scoped to own account_members only
No navigation to household dashboard, settings, Plaid Link, magic actions, or coverage
Audit all existing API routes to confirm requireParent or requireAuth + role check where needed
userStories.testStrategy: API scoping test: kid session returns ONLY their account_members-linked transactions. Negative tests: kid cannot reach /api/accounts, /api/coverage, /api/settings, /api/magic-actions. Kid cannot access sibling data.

userStories.title: Kids balance and transaction view
acceptanceCriteria: Current account balance displayed prominently
Recent transactions list (last 30 days, most recent first)
Each transaction: date, merchant, amount, category
Monthly spending total for current month
Simple, clean design appropriate for teenage users
userStories.testStrategy: Page loads with correct balance and transactions for kid's linked account only. Monthly total calculation test.

userStories.title: Kids category breakdown
acceptanceCriteria: Spending by category for current month using existing household categories
No kid-specific category mapping — uses same categories as parent views (Dining Out, Fast Food, Entertainment, Shopping, etc.)
Parents can add categories as needed (e.g., Home Entertainment for Roblox/PlayStation)
Chart.js visualization (CDN)
Category totals displayed alongside chart
userStories.testStrategy: Category aggregation test scoped to kid's account. Categories match household taxonomy.

userStories.title: Kids monthly budget vs. actual
acceptanceCriteria: Parent-set monthly budget for each kid (admin configuration)
Budget progress bar: spent / total budget
Color coding: green (<70%), yellow (70-99%), red (100%+)
Remaining amount displayed: '$X left this month'
Budget resets monthly
userStories.testStrategy: Budget calculation test. Color threshold test. Monthly reset test.

userStories.title: Money Report Card (LLM narrative)
acceptanceCriteria: Monthly LLM-generated narrative for each kid
Tone: encouraging, educational, age-appropriate (14-16 year olds)
Content: total spent, top categories, biggest purchase, comparison to budget
Example: 'You spent $47 this month. $22 went to food and drinks, $18 to entertainment. Your biggest single purchase was $12 at GameStop.'
Generated on 1st of month, cached in magic_actions_log
Displayed on kids dashboard as a card or collapsible section
No household financial data included in LLM prompt — only kid's first name, their transaction amounts, merchant names, and categories
userStories.testStrategy: Prompt construction test (verify kid-only data, no household info). Mock LLM response rendering test. Tone validation (manual review).

userStories.title: Kids accounts visible on parent accounts screen
acceptanceCriteria: Jordan and Casey's accounts appear on the existing accounts page, broken out like Eric/Alex accounts
Clicking into a kid's account shows their transactions (same drill-down as any other account)
Kids accounts are NOT separate widgets or dashboard sections — they are normal accounts on the accounts screen
Only visible when logged in as a parent
userStories.testStrategy: Parent session sees kids' accounts on accounts page. Kid session does not see parent accounts.

userStories.title: Exclude kids from coverage/liquidity calculations
acceptanceCriteria: coverage-calculator.js filters out accounts linked to kid-role family members via account_members
Kids' depository balances do not inflate household depository_total
Kids have no credit cards or loans — no liability-side changes needed
Coverage API response unchanged for parent sessions; kids don't have access to coverage endpoint
userStories.testStrategy: Coverage calculation test: kid accounts excluded from depository total. Regression test: parent coverage unchanged when kid accounts exist.

high: Data isolation failure = kids see parent financial data — must have test coverage on API-level enforcement, not just UI hiding
medium: Kids may not engage if the UI feels like a 'parent monitoring tool' — design for empowerment, not surveillance
LLM tone for teenagers requires careful prompt engineering — too formal = ignored, too casual = not useful
Existing routes audit: any route missing requireParent is a potential data leak to kid sessions
low: Capital One Money accounts may have limited transaction categorization from Plaid — mitigated by parent-managed category_rules
